title: One noncoding after another: a novel module against late blight in tomato
content: Late blight, an oomycete disease caused by Phytophthora infestans (P. infestans), leads to billions of yearly losses in 2 major Solanaceae crops, tomato and potato. Late blight has a hemibiotrophic life cycle, meaning that it initially lives inside living cells but then switches to a necrotrophic lifestyle that kills the cells it infects. This life cycle makes this disease hard to detect at the early or biotrophic phase when symptoms are mild (Fan et al. 2021), but then it is very hard to control during the later destructive necrotrophic phase (Whisson et al. 2016; Thomas et al. 2024). Traditional breeding and chemical applications have provided limited control of this pathogen because of the complexity of P. infestans populations and their fast evolution. Better understanding late blight should enable speedy and effective innovations to manage this disease.
